# Specification: Bidirectional Relationships with Auto-Generated Inverse Macros

## Capability: bidirectional-relationships

### Version
- **Spec Version**: 1.0.0
- **Last Updated**: 2026-07-19
- **Status**: Draft

---

## Overview

This specification defines the bidirectional relationship capability for the Requirements Traceability Extension. It enables automatic generation of inverse relationships, allowing users to query the traceability graph from both directions without explicitly defining both.

---

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

#### REQ-BID-001: Auto-Generated Inverse Relationships
**Title**: System shall auto-generate inverse relationships for all bidirectional relationship types

**Description**: When a primary relationship is defined (e.g., `addresses:REQ-001[]` in a design), the system shall automatically create the corresponding inverse relationship (e.g., `addressed-by:DES-001` from the requirement to the design).

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Defining `addresses:REQ-001[]` in DES-001 automatically creates `addressed-by:DES-001` relationship from REQ-001
- [ ] Defining `implements:DES-001[]` in IMP-001 automatically creates `implemented-by:IMP-001` relationship from DES-001
- [ ] Defining `composed-of:DES-002[]` in DES-001 automatically creates `part-of:DES-001` relationship from DES-002
- [ ] Defining `depends-on:DES-002[]` in DES-001 automatically creates `depended-by:DES-001` relationship from DES-002
- [ ] All existing relationship types (satisfies, tests, verifies, documents, depends, requires) have corresponding inverses
- [ ] Inverse relationships are marked as `autoGenerated: true`
- [ ] Inverse relationships reference their primary via `inverseOf` property

**Priority**: High
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-002: Bidirectional Query Support
**Title**: System shall support querying relationships from both directions

**Description**: The system shall provide query methods that leverage auto-generated inverse relationships to enable bidirectional queries.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] `getRequirementsForImplementation(implId)` returns all requirements satisfied by the implementation
- [ ] `getImplementationsForRequirement(reqId)` continues to work (existing method)
- [ ] `getRequirementsForDesign(designId)` returns all requirements addressed by the design
- [ ] `getDesignsForRequirement(reqId)` continues to work (existing method)
- [ ] `getImplementationsForDesign(designId)` returns all implementations that implement the design
- [ ] `getDesignsForImplementation(implId)` returns all designs implemented by the implementation
- [ ] `getComposingDesigns(designId)` returns all designs that compose this design (via part-of)
- [ ] `getDependentDesigns(designId)` returns all designs that depend on this design (via depended-by)
- [ ] `getTestsForImplementation(implId)` returns all tests that test this implementation
- [ ] `getImplementationsForTest(testId)` returns all implementations tested by this test
- [ ] `getRequirementsForTest(testId)` returns all requirements verified by this test
- [ ] `getTestsForRequirement(reqId)` continues to work (existing method)
- [ ] `getDocumentsForRequirement(reqId)` returns all documents that document this requirement

**Priority**: High
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-003: Inverse Matrix Generation
**Title**: System shall generate inverse matrices for all bidirectional relationship types

**Description**: The system shall generate new matrix types that show relationships from the inverse direction.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] `matrix-impl-req.csv` shows which requirements each implementation satisfies (via satisfied-by)
- [ ] `matrix-impl-req.html` is generated with styled HTML output
- [ ] `matrix-test-impl.csv` shows which implementations each test tests (via tested-by)
- [ ] `matrix-test-impl.html` is generated with styled HTML output
- [ ] `matrix-test-req.csv` shows which requirements each test verifies (via verified-by)
- [ ] `matrix-test-req.html` is generated with styled HTML output
- [ ] `matrix-design-req.csv` shows which requirements each design addresses (via addressed-by)
- [ ] `matrix-design-req.html` is generated with styled HTML output
- [ ] All inverse matrices have the same format as existing matrices
- [ ] All inverse matrices include summary statistics

**Priority**: High
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-004: Relationship Type Consistency
**Title**: System shall maintain consistency between primary and inverse relationship types

**Description**: The system shall ensure that primary and inverse relationship types are consistently mapped and that the mapping is bidirectional.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] `INVERSE_MAP` maps each primary type to exactly one inverse type
- [ ] `PRIMARY_MAP` maps each inverse type back to its primary type
- [ ] `INVERSE_MAP[PRIMARY_MAP[inverseType]] === inverseType` for all inverse types
- [ ] `PRIMARY_MAP[INVERSE_MAP[primaryType]] === primaryType` for all primary types
- [ ] All relationship types (primary and inverse) are valid `RelationshipType` values

**Priority**: High
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-005: Duplicate Prevention
**Title**: System shall prevent duplicate relationship definitions

**Description**: The system shall ensure that each relationship (in either direction) is stored only once, preventing duplicates.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Attempting to add a relationship that already exists (same fromId, type, targetId) throws an error
- [ ] If a primary relationship exists, attempting to add its inverse explicitly generates a warning and replaces the existing inverse
- [ ] If an inverse relationship exists, attempting to add its primary explicitly generates a warning and replaces the existing primary
- [ ] Each relationship has a unique ID based on `fromId-type-targetId`

**Priority**: Medium
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-006: Circular Reference Detection
**Title**: System shall detect and report circular references

**Description**: The system shall detect circular references in the relationship graph and report them as warnings during validation.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] `validate()` method detects circular references
- [ ] Circular references are reported as warnings (not errors)
- [ ] Circular reference detection works for all relationship types
- [ ] Circular reference detection has configurable depth limit to prevent infinite loops
- [ ] Circular reference warnings include the full cycle path

**Priority**: Medium
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-007: Backward Compatibility
**Title**: System shall maintain 100% backward compatibility with existing code

**Description**: All existing functionality shall continue to work without modification after implementing bidirectional relationships.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] All existing tests pass without modification
- [ ] Existing query methods return the same results as before
- [ ] Existing matrices are generated with the same data as before
- [ ] Existing relationship parsing works unchanged
- [ ] Existing graph storage works unchanged
- [ ] No breaking changes to public APIs

**Priority**: High
**Status**: Approved

---

#### REQ-BID-008: Performance Requirements
**Title**: System shall maintain O(1) query performance for both primary and inverse relationship queries

**Description**: Query performance shall not degrade when using inverse relationships.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] `getRelationships(nodeId, type)` returns in O(1) average time for both primary and inverse types
- [ ] All convenience methods (getRequirementsForImplementation, etc.) return in O(1) average time
- [ ] Relationship storage uses O(n) space where n is the number of primary relationships (2n total including inverses)
- [ ] For 1000 primary relationships, memory usage increase is < 1MB
- [ ] For 1000 primary relationships, query time increase is < 10ms

**Priority**: High
**Status**: Approved

---

## Relationship Types

### Primary Relationship Types (User-Defined)

| Type | Direction | Description | Inverse Type |
|------|-----------|-------------|--------------|
| `satisfies` | Implementation → Requirement | Implementation satisfies a requirement | `satisfied-by` |
| `tests` | Test → Implementation | Test tests an implementation | `tested-by` |
| `verifies` | Test → Requirement | Test verifies a requirement | `verified-by` |
| `documents` | Document → Requirement | Document documents a requirement | `documented-by` |
| `depends` | Any → Any | Generic dependency relationship | `depended-by` |
| `requires` | Any → Any | Generic requirement relationship | `required-by` |
| `addresses` | Design → Requirement | Design addresses a requirement | `addressed-by` |
| `implements` | Implementation → Design | Implementation implements a design | `implemented-by` |
| `composed-of` | Design → Design | Design is composed of other designs | `part-of` |
| `depends-on` | Design → Design | Design depends on other designs | `depended-by` |

### Inverse Relationship Types (Auto-Generated)

| Type | Direction | Description | Primary Type |
|------|-----------|-------------|--------------|
| `satisfied-by` | Requirement → Implementation | Requirement is satisfied by an implementation | `satisfies` |
| `tested-by` | Implementation → Test | Implementation is tested by a test | `tests` |
| `verified-by` | Requirement → Test | Requirement is verified by a test | `verifies` |
| `documented-by` | Requirement → Document | Requirement is documented by a document | `documents` |
| `depended-by` | Any → Any | Node is depended on by another node | `depends` |
| `required-by` | Any → Any | Node is required by another node | `requires` |
| `addressed-by` | Requirement → Design | Requirement is addressed by a design | `addresses` |
| `implemented-by` | Design → Implementation | Design is implemented by an implementation | `implements` |
| `part-of` | Design → Design | Design is part of another design | `composed-of` |
| `depended-by` | Design → Design | Design is depended on by another design | `depends-on` |

---

## Data Model

### Relationship Interface

```typescript
interface Relationship {
  /** Unique identifier for this relationship */
  id: string;

  /** Source node ID */
  fromId: string;

  /** Target node ID */
  targetId: string;

  /** Relationship type (primary or inverse) */
  type: RelationshipType;

  /** Source file where this relationship was defined */
  sourceFile?: string;

  /** Line number in source file */
  line?: number;

  /** Whether this relationship was auto-generated as an inverse */
  autoGenerated: boolean;

  /** ID of the primary relationship this is an inverse of (if auto-generated) */
  inverseOf?: string;
}
```

### Relationship Type Definitions

```typescript
type PrimaryRelationshipType =
  | 'satisfies' | 'tests' | 'verifies' | 'documents'
  | 'depends' | 'requires' | 'addresses' | 'implements'
  | 'composed-of' | 'depends-on';

type InverseRelationshipType =
  | 'satisfied-by' | 'tested-by' | 'verified-by' | 'documented-by'
  | 'depended-by' | 'required-by' | 'addressed-by' | 'implemented-by'
  | 'part-of' | 'depended-by';

type RelationshipType = PrimaryRelationshipType | InverseRelationshipType;
```

### Mapping Constants

```typescript
const INVERSE_MAP: Record<PrimaryRelationshipType, InverseRelationshipType> = {
  'satisfies': 'satisfied-by',
  'tests': 'tested-by',
  'verifies': 'verified-by',
  'documents': 'documented-by',
  'depends': 'depended-by',
  'requires': 'required-by',
  'addresses': 'addressed-by',
  'implements': 'implemented-by',
  'composed-of': 'part-of',
  'depends-on': 'depended-by',
};

const PRIMARY_MAP: Record<InverseRelationshipType, PrimaryRelationshipType> = {
  'satisfied-by': 'satisfies',
  'tested-by': 'tests',
  'verified-by': 'verifies',
  'documented-by': 'documents',
  'depended-by': 'depends',
  'required-by': 'requires',
  'addressed-by': 'addresses',
  'implemented-by': 'implements',
  'part-of': 'composed-of',
  'depended-by': 'depends-on',
};
```

## API Specification

### Query Methods

#### getRequirementsForImplementation(implId: string): Requirement[]
Returns all requirements that are satisfied by the given implementation.

**Parameters:**
- `implId`: The ID of the implementation

**Returns:** Array of Requirement objects

**Example:**
```typescript
const reqs = graph.getRequirementsForImplementation('IMP-001');
// Returns: [REQ-001, REQ-002]
```

---

#### getImplementationsForDesign(designId: string): Implementation[]
Returns all implementations that implement the given design.

**Parameters:**
- `designId`: The ID of the design

**Returns:** Array of Implementation objects

**Example:**
```typescript
const impls = graph.getImplementationsForDesign('DES-001');
// Returns: [IMP-001, IMP-002]
```

---

#### getRequirementsForDesign(designId: string): Requirement[]
Returns all requirements that are addressed by the given design.

**Parameters:**
- `designId`: The ID of the design

**Returns:** Array of Requirement objects

**Example:**
```typescript
const reqs = graph.getRequirementsForDesign('DES-001');
// Returns: [REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003]
```

---

#### getDesignsForImplementation(implId: string): Design[]
Returns all designs that are implemented by the given implementation.

**Parameters:**
- `implId`: The ID of the implementation

**Returns:** Array of Design objects

**Example:**
```typescript
const designs = graph.getDesignsForImplementation('IMP-001');
// Returns: [DES-001]
```

---

#### getComposingDesigns(designId: string): Design[]
Returns all designs that compose (are parents of) the given design.

**Parameters:**
- `designId`: The ID of the design

**Returns:** Array of Design objects

**Example:**
```typescript
const parents = graph.getComposingDesigns('DES-002');
// Returns: [DES-001]  (if DES-001 composed-of DES-002)
```

---

#### getDependentDesigns(designId: string): Design[]
Returns all designs that depend on the given design.

**Parameters:**
- `designId`: The ID of the design

**Returns:** Array of Design objects

**Example:**
```typescript
const dependents = graph.getDependentDesigns('DES-001');
// Returns: [DES-002, DES-003]  (if they depend-on DES-001)
```

---

### Matrix Types

#### Standard Matrices (Existing)
- `matrix-req-impl.csv/html` - Requirements to Implementations (satisfies)
- `matrix-req-test.csv/html` - Requirements to Tests (verifies)
- `matrix-req-design.csv/html` - Requirements to Designs (addresses)
- `matrix-design-impl.csv/html` - Designs to Implementations (implements)
- `matrix-full.csv/html` - Full traceability matrix

#### Inverse Matrices (New)
- `matrix-impl-req.csv/html` - Implementations to Requirements (satisfied-by)
- `matrix-test-impl.csv/html` - Tests to Implementations (tested-by)
- `matrix-test-req.csv/html` - Tests to Requirements (verified-by)
- `matrix-design-req.csv/html` - Designs to Requirements (addressed-by)

---

## Validation Rules

### VR-BID-001: Relationship ID Uniqueness
Each relationship (identified by `fromId-type-targetId`) must be unique.

**Error Message:** `Duplicate relationship: {fromId} {type} {targetId}`

**Severity:** Error

---

### VR-BID-002: Node Existence
Both source and target nodes of a relationship must exist.

**Warning Message:** `Relationship {type} references non-existent node: {nodeId}`

**Severity:** Warning

---

### VR-BID-003: Circular Reference Detection
Circular references should be detected and reported.

**Warning Message:** `Circular reference detected: {path}`

**Severity:** Warning

---

### VR-BID-004: Inverse Consistency
If a primary relationship exists, its inverse must also exist (auto-generated).

**Error Message:** `Inconsistent relationship state: primary exists without inverse`

**Severity:** Error (internal consistency check)

---

## Examples

### Example 1: Basic Bidirectional Relationship

**Input:**
```asciidoc
[design, id=DES-001, title="Authentication System"]
====
The authentication system design.
addresses:REQ-001,REQ-002[]
====

[req, id=REQ-001, title="User Authentication"]
====
Users must be able to authenticate.
====

[req, id=REQ-002, title="Password Management"]
====
Users must be able to manage passwords.
====

[imp, id=IMP-001, title="Auth Service"]
====
Authentication service implementation.
implements:DES-001[]
====
```

**Auto-Generated Inverses:**
- `REQ-001` has `addressed-by:DES-001`
- `REQ-002` has `addressed-by:DES-001`
- `DES-001` has `implemented-by:IMP-001`

**Query Results:**
- `getRequirementsForDesign('DES-001')` → `[REQ-001, REQ-002]`
- `getDesignsForRequirement('REQ-001')` → `[DES-001]`
- `getImplementationsForDesign('DES-001')` → `[IMP-001]`
- `getDesignsForImplementation('IMP-001')` → `[DES-001]`

---

### Example 2: Design Composition

**Input:**
```asciidoc
[design, id=DES-001, title="System Architecture"]
====
Overall system architecture.
composed-of:DES-002,DES-003[]
====

[design, id=DES-002, title="Frontend"]
====
Frontend components.
====

[design, id=DES-003, title="Backend"]
====
Backend services.
====
```

**Auto-Generated Inverses:**
- `DES-002` has `part-of:DES-001`
- `DES-003` has `part-of:DES-001`

**Query Results:**
- `getComposingDesigns('DES-002')` → `[DES-001]`
- `getComposingDesigns('DES-003')` → `[DES-001]`
- `getDesignsComposedOf('DES-001')` → `[DES-002, DES-003]` (existing method)

---

### Example 3: Matrix Output

**Input:** Same as Example 1

**matrix-req-design.csv:**
```csv
Requirement ID,Requirement Title,DES-001,Status
REQ-001,User Authentication,✓,✓ Complete
REQ-002,Password Management,✓,✓ Complete

Total Requirements,2
Requirements with Designs,2
Design Coverage,100%
```

**matrix-design-req.csv (NEW):**
```csv
Design ID,Design Title,REQ-001,REQ-002,Status
DES-001,Authentication System,✓,✓,✓ Complete

Total Designs,1
Designs with Requirements,1
Requirement Coverage by Design,100%
```

## Performance Characteristics

| Operation | Time Complexity | Space Complexity | Notes |
|-----------|-----------------|------------------|-------|
| Add relationship | O(1) | O(1) | Includes inverse generation |
| Query by type | O(1) | O(1) | Uses index maps |
| Query all relationships for node | O(1) | O(1) | Uses relationship map |
| Validate graph | O(n + m) | O(n + m) | n = nodes, m = relationships |
| Detect circular references | O(n + m) | O(n) | DFS traversal |

---

## Constraints

1. **Relationship ID Format**: `{fromId}-{type}-{targetId}`
2. **Inverse ID Format**: `{targetId}-{inverseType}-{fromId}`
3. **Maximum Relationships**: No hard limit, but performance degrades with very large graphs (>10,000 relationships)
4. **Circular Reference Depth**: Default maximum depth of 100 for cycle detection
